== ASSIGNMENT RULES XML FORMAT == There are TWO assignment rule files — one per object: Lead rules → assignmentRules/Lead.assignmentRules (memberName: Lead) Case rules → assignmentRules/Case.assignmentRules (memberName: Case) metadataType: AssignmentRules ALL rules for the same object go into ONE file — never split them.
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <AssignmentRules xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <assignmentRule> <fullName>RuleName</fullName> <active>true</active> <!-- ruleEntry with criteria --> <ruleEntry> <assignedTo>john.doe@company.com</assignedTo> <assignedToType>User</assignedToType> <criteriaItems> <field>Lead.Country</field> <operation>equals</operation> <value>US,USA,United States</value> </criteriaItems> </ruleEntry> <!-- ruleEntry with formula --> <ruleEntry> <assignedTo>Lead_Queue</assignedTo> <assignedToType>Queue</assignedToType> <formula>ISBLANK( Email )</formula> </ruleEntry> <!-- ruleEntry with NO criteria at all — catches everything not matched above. See CATCH-ALL section below. MUST be the last ruleEntry in the block. --> <ruleEntry> <assignedTo>Lead_Queue</assignedTo> <assignedToType>Queue</assignedToType> </ruleEntry> </assignmentRule> </AssignmentRules>
== ASSIGNMENT RULES RULES ==
-- STRUCTURE -- - Don't add user unless it is explicitly provided in the ticket — never fabricate usernames - One file per object: Lead or Case — NEVER combine Lead and Case in same file - ALL rules for the same object go in ONE file with multiple <assignmentRule> blocks - Each <assignmentRule> has <fullName>, <active>, and one or more <ruleEntry> blocks - <criteriaItems> and <formula> are mutually exclusive per ruleEntry — never use both
-- RULE ENTRY ORDER (CRITICAL) -- - <ruleEntry> blocks are evaluated TOP TO BOTTOM at runtime. A record is assigned by the FIRST entry whose criteria match, and evaluation stops there — later entries never see that record. Always emit specific/narrow entries FIRST and any catch-all/default entry LAST.
-- CATCH-ALL / "ALL REMAINING" / "EVERYONE ELSE" ENTRIES (CRITICAL) -- When the ticket describes a default bucket — "all remaining Leads", "everyone else", "any other [value]", "anything not covered above" — represent it as a <ruleEntry> with NO <criteriaItems>, NO <formula>, and NO <booleanFilter>: just <assignedTo> and <assignedToType>. An empty-criteria ruleEntry matches every record that reaches it, which (combined with rule-entry order above) is exactly "all remaining" — this entry MUST be the LAST <ruleEntry> in the <assignmentRule>. - NEVER emulate "all remaining" by building a formula/booleanFilter that negates every other branch (e.g. chaining NOT(...) AND NOT(...) AND ... once per other value). This is the most common cause of "Syntax error. Extra AND" / "Extra OR" deploy failures on this metadata type: the negated list gets built by iterating the other branches and an operator is left dangling at the end with nothing after it to join. It's also unnecessary — an empty-criteria last entry does the same job with no formula at all. - Worked example — ticket: "Web → Mahesh Pawar, Partner Referral → Sales Lead Queue, Purchased List → Integration User, all remaining → Lead Queue": WRONG (produces "Extra AND" on deploy): <formula>NOT(ISPICKVAL(LeadSource,'Web')) AND NOT(ISPICKVAL(LeadSource,'Partner Referral')) AND NOT(ISPICKVAL(LeadSource,'Purchased List')) AND</formula> CORRECT: emit three <ruleEntry> blocks with <criteriaItems> for Web / Partner Referral / Purchased List (in that order), then a fourth <ruleEntry> with no criteria at all assigned to Lead Queue, placed last.
-- BOOLEAN FILTER (only when a ruleEntry genuinely needs OR / mixed logic) -- - Default (no <booleanFilter> present) = AND across all <criteriaItems> in that ruleEntry. Multiple <criteriaItems> in one ruleEntry with no booleanFilter = AND; separate <ruleEntry> blocks = OR between whole rules. - Only add <booleanFilter> when the ticket explicitly needs OR or a mix within a SINGLE ruleEntry (e.g. "A or B, both also requiring C"). Its value is a 1-indexed expression referencing <criteriaItems> by position, e.g. "1 OR 2" or "1 AND (2 OR 3)". - The indexes used MUST exactly match the number of <criteriaItems> present in that same ruleEntry — every index 1..N appears exactly once, joined by AND/OR between them. - NEVER leave a trailing or leading AND/OR, NEVER emit two operators back to back, and NEVER reference an index that doesn't exist — Salesforce reports these as "Syntax error. Extra AND", "Extra OR", or "Number of criteria doesn't match". - If every ruleEntry in the file only needs plain AND (the common case, including the single-criterion case), omit <booleanFilter> entirely — don't add it "just in case".
-- ACTIVE RULE -- - Only ONE rule per object can be active=true at a time - If ticket says "activate" a rule, set that rule active=true and ALL other rules active=false - If creating a new rule and ticket says it should be active: set active=true and set ALL existing rules to active=false
-- ASSIGNED TO -- - assignedToType: User or Queue - If User: match the ticket's person name against orgState.existingUsers by Name and use that user's exact username (email format) as the value — NEVER fabricate or guess a username. If no match is found, do NOT deploy a guessed value — return an error in summary naming the unresolved person instead. - If Queue: assignedTo = Queue DeveloperName, NOT its display label (e.g. "Sales Lead Queue" → Sales_Lead_Queue). Match against orgState.existingQueues by name/label to get the real DeveloperName rather than transforming the label yourself — a guessed DeveloperName that doesn't exist in the org fails deploy with "no Queue named X found". If no match is found, do NOT guess — return an error in summary naming the unresolved queue instead.
-- CRITERIA ITEMS -- - field format: ObjectName.FieldApiName (e.g. Lead.Country, Case.Status) - operation values: equals, notEqual, contains, notContain, startsWith, greaterThan, greaterOrEqual, lessThan, lessOrEqual, isNull - value: comma-separated for multiple values
-- FORMULA -- - ALWAYS XML-escape formula characters: < → < > → > & → & - Example: ISBLANK( Email ), NOT(ISBLANK( Country__c )) - Before emitting any formula built by joining multiple conditions (AND/OR), re-read it and confirm it ends in a condition, not a trailing operator, and that no two operators appear back to back — a dangling AND/OR is the direct cause of "Syntax error. Extra AND"/"Extra OR" deploy failures (see the CATCH-ALL section above for the most common way this happens).
-- CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE -- - For CREATE or UPDATE tickets: preserve ALL existing rules exactly as they are — never drop or alter a rule the ticket didn't mention, just because the whole file is being regenerated. - CRITICAL — DELETING AN EXISTING ASSIGNMENT RULE IS NOT POSSIBLE THROUGH ANY MECHANISM THIS TOOL HAS ACCESS TO. This was verified directly against a live org, not assumed: regenerating the file with the target rule's <assignmentRule> block omitted does NOT remove it, deploying a destructiveFiles/destructiveChanges entry for it does NOT remove it (delete() isn't supported for this type), and deploying a completely EMPTY AssignmentRules file does NOT remove ANY existing rule either — a live test confirmed all existing rules were still present and unchanged afterward. Salesforce's Metadata API deploy for this type only ever ADDS a new named rule or UPDATES one already named in the file; anything already in the org that the deployed file simply doesn't mention is left completely untouched, no matter how the file is built. The ONLY way to actually remove an assignment rule is a human clicking "Del" next to it in Setup → Lead/Case Assignment Rules — there is no API path to it at all. - Therefore, when a ticket asks to DELETE or remove one or more assignment rules: → Do NOT generate a "files" entry or a "destructiveFiles" entry for the rule(s) to be deleted — there is nothing deployable that accomplishes this, and generating XML that looks like a valid regeneration would misreport the deletion as done when it silently isn't (this happened repeatedly before this limitation was confirmed). → Set the summary to plainly state which rule(s) cannot be deleted and why, e.g.: "Salesforce does not support deleting Assignment Rules via the Metadata API — 'Email Domain Routing' must be removed manually via Setup → Lead Assignment Rules → Del." Do not phrase this as a generic failure — say specifically that it's a Salesforce platform limitation, not a mistake in the request. → If the SAME ticket also asks for other changes that ARE achievable (e.g. "delete rule X and activate rule Y"), still generate and deploy those other changes normally — only the deletion portion is impossible, and it must not block unrelated achievable work in the same ticket. → Deactivating a rule (<active>false</active>) is a real, achievable, different action from deleting it — do NOT silently substitute deactivation when the ticket explicitly says delete/remove. Only treat "remove" as deactivation if the ticket's own wording is genuinely ambiguous between "stop it from running" and "delete the record" — and even then, say in the summary that you interpreted it as deactivation and why, so the requester can correct you if that's not what they meant.
